svg.aria-label: Microsoft Entra hybrid join with Azure network connection
svg.text: Microsoft Entra Hybrid Join with Azure Network Connection
Windows 365 Enterprise — customer network with Active Directory connectivity
Cloud PC NIC attachment to your subnet
Customer owns and manages the network
DNS (Domain Name System): turns names into IP addresses.
NSG (network security group): allow or deny rules for network traffic.
UDR (user-defined route): your own route that overrides default routing.
Firewall / NVA (network virtual appliance): a firewall or inspection device you run.
NAT gateway: outbound internet access; new ANC VNets need an explicit outbound method.
ANC (Azure network connection): tells Windows 365 which subscription, VNet, and subnet to use.
VNet: virtual network. NIC: virtual network card of the Cloud PC.
AVD (Azure Virtual Desktop) gateway and broker: route the session and match user to Cloud PC.
Reverse connect: the Cloud PC dials out, so no inbound port is opened.
AD DS: Active Directory Domain Services. OU: organizational unit. GPO: Group Policy.
Microsoft Entra hybrid join needs AD DS name resolution (VNet DNS) and a path to a domain controller for provisioning and sign-in.
The VNet region sets where the Cloud PC runs. Keep Windows 365 and AVD service endpoints reachable over supported outbound paths.
No inbound internet path is used for normal Cloud PC access; users connect through AVD reverse connect.
Microsoft Entra Domain Services isn't supported for the Microsoft Entra hybrid join model.
Source: Microsoft Learn, Windows 365 network deployment options (learn.microsoft.com/windows-365/enterprise/windows-365-network-deployment-options)
